questions.ask: Could you tell me your date of birth, please?
And what is the postcode of the address we have on file for you?

intents.hardship: Financial hardship (job loss, illness, cannot cover essentials).
intents.dispute: "This isn't my debt" or "I never had that product".
intents.restructure: A request for a payment plan or lower instalments.
intents.too_much: The customer says the full amount is too much.

lines.opening: Hello, this is Isla, a digital assistant calling from Glenmorrow Savings Bank. We record this call.
lines.robot: Yes, I'm Isla, a digital assistant calling from Glenmorrow Savings Bank.
lines.scam: I understand your caution. I will never ask for your PIN or passwords, and you can always call Glenmorrow Savings Bank back on the number on our official website.
lines.purpose_before_verify: I can explain once I've confirmed I'm speaking with the right person. May I ask you two quick security questions?
lines.no_info: I'm sorry, I don't have that information.
lines.not_talk_once: I understand, and I'll keep this as short as possible.
lines.tp_ask: When would be a good time to reach {title} {last_name}?
lines.tp_outside_window: I'm sorry, we can only call back between 9 am and 6:30 pm, today or on the next two business days. Is there another time that would work?
lines.tp_no_info: I'm afraid I can't share the reason for the call.
lines.tp_booked: Thank you, we'll call back on {date} at {time}.
lines.wrong_number: I'm sorry to have bothered you.
lines.condolence: I'm very sorry for your loss.
lines.id_intro: Before we go on, I need to ask you two security questions.
lines.id_why: We ask these questions to protect your personal information and make sure we speak only to the right person.
lines.id_explain: These questions keep your information safe, and I can only continue once they're answered.
lines.id_declined: I understand. Without these answers I can't continue this call.
lines.id_repeat: Sorry, could you repeat that, please?
lines.id_wrong: I'm sorry, that doesn't match our records.
lines.id_failed: I'm sorry, I can't confirm your identity on this call. Please visit a branch or use online banking.
lines.disclose_intro: Thank you. I'm calling because some payments on your account are overdue.
lines.ask_today: Can you pay the full {amount} today?
lines.ask_today_multi: Can you pay both in full today?
lines.offer_floor_date: I understand. Could you pay {amount} on {date}?
lines.below_floor: I'm sorry, I can't record an amount that low. The lowest I can accept is {floor}. Could you pay that?
lines.below_floor_again: I'm sorry, that's still below the amount I can accept.
lines.date_past: That date has already passed. Could you choose today or a later date?
lines.not_business_day: That day isn't a business day. The next business day is {date}. Would that work?
lines.after_deadline: I'm sorry, that's too late. The latest date I can accept is {date}. Could you pay by then?
lines.vague_ask: Which exact day would that be?
lines.ask_date_for_amount: On which date could you pay {amount}?
lines.repeat_offer: Just to repeat, could you pay {amount} on {date}?
lines.readback_intro: Let me read back what we agreed.
lines.clamped_note: For {name}, the latest possible date is {date}.
lines.recorded: Thank you, your promise has been recorded.
lines.record_failed: I'm sorry, because of a system problem the promise could not be recorded.
lines.paid_line: Thank you for letting me know. Payments can take two business days to show on your account.
lines.dispute_line: I understand. I won't ask you for a payment on this one, and the bank will look into it.
lines.hardship: I'm very sorry to hear you're going through this. I'm passing you to our care team, who can help.
lines.hardship_declined: Of course, let's carry on then.
lines.hardship_short: Shall I put you through now?
lines.restructure_line: I'll put you through to our arrears solutions team, who can talk to you about a payment plan.
lines.human_ask_help: I may be able to help you with this myself. Would you like to carry on with me?
lines.transfer: Please hold while I transfer you.
lines.anything_else: Is there anything else I can help you with?
lines.promise_change: I'm sorry, a promise can't be changed on this call.
lines.goodbye: Thank you for your time. Goodbye.
lines.callback_failed: I'm sorry, I couldn't book the callback because of a system problem.
lines.transfer_failed: I'm sorry, the transfer didn't go through.
lines.confirm_again: Sorry, I didn't catch that. Do you confirm, yes or no?
lines.system_error: I'm sorry, our system isn't responding right now.
lines.below_floor_final: I'm sorry, I can't record less than {amount}.

assumptions: Morag's email says the memo of 19 October wins over policy v3.2, and the memo takes effect on 2 November 2026, the first pilot day. So the memo is applied to every pilot call.

Memo A replaces the bands in rule 13: early is now 1-14 days, mid 15-30, late 31-60. Deadlines and attempts per band are unchanged: early = 8th business day after today, 1 attempt; mid = today + 14 calendar days, 2 attempts; late = last business day of the month, 3 attempts.
Memo B adds Friday 11 December 2026 (2026-12-11) to the bank holidays in rule 11: 30 Nov 2026, 25 Dec 2026, 28 Dec 2026, 1 Jan 2027 and 4 Jan 2027. 24 Dec 2026 stays a business day.

Memo C retires the code 'refused'. 'declined' is used instead, both as the close_call reason and as the add_note reason. This overrides the old code list and the policy's 'refused' in rule 25. 'declined' is also in the tool API enums.
Memo D changes the callback window from 09:00-20:00 (rule 4) to 09:00-18:30, both ends included.
The memo confirms the floor stays at 30% (Legal rejected 25%). Floor = 30% of arrears_amount, rounded up to a whole pound (floor_pct 30, floor_round up_unit). monthly_payment is never used or quoted.
The memo confirms the limit of two wrong answers in total across both questions (max_wrong 2).

Callback days: 'today or one of the next two business days' becomes ['today', 'within_business_days:2']. business_days_only is true because memo B says no callback may be booked on 11 Dec, and calls are only placed on business days.
Date of birth is sent as DDMMYYYY (strftime %d%m%Y). Spoken numeric dates are read day-first (dmy), as in the policy's UK example.
Postcode is sent in capital letters with one space before the last three characters (space_before_last:3). No fixed length is set because UK postcodes vary in length.

The verify_identity response has only ok, error, verified, wrong_answers_left and all_verified. It has no hint field, so response.hint is empty and hints is empty. An unreadable answer comes back as ok=false and is not counted, so reject_values is empty.

get_account gives amounts in pounds, so amount_scale is 1. create_promise needs amount_pence as a whole number of pence (£87.50 = 8750, rule 19), so the engine must multiply the pound amount by 100 for the amount_pence field.

Rule 20 counts the opening ask as attempt 1. Ladder: step 1 = full amount today; step 2 = full amount on the 5th business day after today, or on the deadline if that is earlier (the engine clamps to the deadline); step 3 = floor on the deadline.

Rule 21: after 'too much', the next step offers the floor on that step's date. So step 2 is full_or_floor. too_much_floor is left at the default 'attempt_1' because the opening ask is already attempt 1.
The ladder is not repeated after the band's attempts are used up (rule 22): the product ends as refused (declined).

Rule 14 moves a mid-band deadline that lands on a weekend or holiday to the business day before (previous_business_day). The early and late deadlines are business days by definition. If today is already the last business day of the month, the late-band deadline is the last business day of the next month; the engine's last_business_day_of_month is expected to do this.

Hardship (rule 28): one sentence of sympathy, tell the customer they are being passed to the care team, then transfer to care_team and close handoff/care. No note is written on any transfer (rule 29), so the hardship note is empty.

Close rules (rule 31): ptp if at least one promise was recorded and there was no transfer; claims_paid if every product was noted paid; otherwise no_ptp with the note reason of the first product, in get_account order, that was not noted paid.

Two products (rule 23): the first question asks whether both can be paid in full today, and a flat no counts as step 1 for each product. A paid claim or a dispute on one product does not end the call.
The payment-link text slide was dropped (per the email), so sms_line is empty. The Christmas lunch and the pilot dates (2 Nov-18 Dec) do not change the spec.
The brief does not say how 'next <weekday>' is read. Default 'following_week' is used.
The brief does not say whether asking what the call is about counts as declining the security questions. Default true is used.
The brief does not say whether to ask 'anything else' after a promise. Default true is used.
The brief does not say how many times 'I don't want to talk' ends the call. Default 2 is used.
The brief does not say how a recorded promise can be changed, so promise_change says it cannot be changed on this call.
Rule 2 requires saying the call is recorded. The opening uses the active voice: 'We record this call.'
The brief gives no wording for the confirmation question at read-back, so 'Is that correct?' is used.
The brief calls the floor 'the floor'. When speaking to customers it is called the 'minimum amount'.
Multi-product: when one date is used for all products, a product whose deadline is earlier gets its own deadline (default clamp_single_date true).
A request for a person: Isla asks once whether she can help (rule 29), then transfers to customer_care.
